close_reason: Fixed in 35b8a9d (docs only): both metadata fields now document the discriminator-keyed schema, cite the spec's 'Clients MUST ignore unknown keys' contract, and direct consumers to from_value at their boundary. Confirmed against the draft text that the value shape is deliberately left open per type, so the doc-clarification path (not a typed companion module) is the correct resolution.
description:
SECTION: Contract underspecification

CONTRACT RISK
Two public fields carry the Sloppy-Value shape
(Option<serde_json::Value>) but with significantly weaker contract
than the workspace's sanctioned use of that pattern:

  src/message.rs  MessageAction.metadata: Option<serde_json::Value>
                  /// The `metadata` property (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.3).

  src/contact.rs  Endpoint.metadata: Option<serde_json::Value>
                  /// Arbitrary provider-defined metadata.

Workspace AGENTS.md authorises Sloppy-Value for "fields whose value
shape is defined by an external IETF spec (JSCalendar / RFC 8984,
JSContact / RFC 9553, etc.) and is large or extensible", AND
mandates the hybrid pattern: "keep the public field as
serde_json::Value for round-trip fidelity, and add parallel typed
sub-types in a sibling module (e.g. jscalendar.rs)".

The two fields above are NOT covered by the IETF-external-spec
exception:
- MessageAction.metadata is defined by draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.3
  itself (the same draft this crate implements), not an external
  spec. No parallel typed module exists.
- Endpoint.metadata is explicitly "provider-defined" — no spec at
  all, just per-provider extensions.

WHAT BREAKS FOR CALLERS
- Cross-implementation interop: a client built against this crate
  receiving a MessageAction with metadata from a different vendor's
  server cannot tell from the type whether the JSON value is
  expected to match any schema. The caller writes its own
  serde_json::from_value::<AcmeCorpMetadata>(v) on every site.
- Server-side validation: a server using these types to validate an
  inbound /set request has no schema to compare against. The crate
  punts validation entirely.
- Round-trip is preserved, but semantic correctness is not.

The mode-prompt review did not flag this. The closest existing
finding is JMAP-ly0n.5 (URI-latitude doc on ChatContact.id), which
addresses doc precision rather than the schema-discovery gap on
metadata fields.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM CALENDARS/CONTACTS
jmap-calendars-types and jmap-contacts-types receive their
sloppy-value approval BECAUSE they consume RFC 8984 / RFC 9553 and
expose parallel typed sub-types in jscalendar / jscontact modules
(per crate-jmap-calendars-types/PLAN.md §1-§8,
crate-jmap-contacts-types/PLAN.md §10). The workspace pattern is
"sloppy-Value field + typed companion module".

chat-types ships neither end of that pattern for these two fields:
no spec citation that pins down the value shape (MessageAction) or
no spec at all (Endpoint), and no typed companion module.

RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION
For MessageAction.metadata:
- If the JMAP Chat draft §4.3 enumerates expected schemas keyed by
  the `type` field (the existing MessageAction.action_type: "button"
  | "link" | …), add a sibling module action_metadata.rs with a typed
  enum or per-action-type struct. Same pattern as the
  jscalendar.rs / jscontact.rs companion modules.
- If §4.3 deliberately leaves the value shape open, add a doc clause
  saying so explicitly and pointing callers at the action_type field
  as the discriminant they MUST switch on.

For Endpoint.metadata:
- Add a doc clause naming the federation drafts that define
  per-endpoint-type metadata schemas (XMPP, SIP, email, etc.) or
  citing where vendors are expected to publish their schemas.
- Alternatively, demote to Option<serde_json::Map<String, Value>>
  to align with the workspace `extra` pattern semantics (vendor
  catch-all rather than typed payload).

ORACLE
Workspace AGENTS.md "Sloppy-Value pattern for IETF-defined nested
objects" section; crate-jmap-calendars-types/PLAN.md §1-§8;
crate-jmap-contacts-types/PLAN.md §10.
title: MessageAction.metadata and Endpoint.metadata are unconstrained sloppy-Value fields without typed companion or schema reference
